schema: Gold ground-truth annotations. Anchors resolved in reference_text() (resolve=last→rfind; <<EOF>>=EOF). structure=repeating ⇒ expected_count+count_cue carry cardinality (A3 scores recall-of-count, not exact edges); exemplars anchor concrete instances. role=primary drives the rating; role=secondary is a grouping level reported but not rated. Offsets derived at eval time, never stored. NOTE (Phase-2): per-instance character EDGES for idx101 are produced programmatically by the column-aware geometry parser (.scratch/mask-eval/lds_extract.py), NOT hand-stored here — the linear reference_text() interleaves the footnote apparatus before each chapter, so stored offsets against it are meaningless. See ratification-results.md → idx101 for the reference_text() decision this implies.

The 5 single-chapter BoM books (Enos, Jarom, Omni, Words of Mormon, 4 Nephi) and 3 single-chapter PoGP books (JS—Matthew, JS—History, Articles of Faith) print NO 'Chapter 1' label — they run straight into verses; their single chapter is implicit. 384 explicit 'Chapter N'/'Section N' labels recovered by geometry parse (385 expected for the labeled chapters; the 1-label shortfall is a degraded/wrapped label, flagged in ratification-results.md).

D&C: a section header summarizing the verse ranges before verse 1, cued as 'Section N' ×138. Total ≈ 393 (= chapter count): 384 explicit 'Chapter N'/'Section N' labels recovered by the column-aware geometry parse + 8 single-chapter book-level summaries (the 8 label-less single-chapter books carry a book-argument summary in the heading slot). PRIOR contract left this null ('PDF degradation makes the BoM half not cleanly countable') — the geometry parse (lds_extract.py) RESOLVES the scramble and makes it countable; remaining 1-label shortfall vs 385 documented as a degraded/wrapped heading.

annotations.count_cue: Per-page cross-reference apparatus: a 3-column footnote band at the bottom of nearly every verse page, keyed to inline superscript letters (a, b, c…) in the verse body. Geometrically isolable — the middle footnote column starts at x0≈159, an x-band the verse body never uses. The naive linear extraction emits this band BEFORE the chapter it annotates (the core scramble). NOT exemplar-anchorable by content: apparatus entries reuse Topical-Guide targets (e.g. 'Record Keeping' recurs 28×, 'tg Birthright.' 3×), so no footnote string resolves uniquely. Presence + clean geometric separation from body is the requirement; per-instance edges come from the geometry parser, not reference_text().
annotations.note: NEW in Phase-2 ratification. The footnote apparatus is a distinct masked layer the linear pipeline had folded into chapter/body text. Recoverable only via the geometry parse, not from reference_text() ordering.

Type=front_matter because these are prefatory matter to the BoM volume (printed before 1 Nephi), not back matter — placed by where the anchor resolves (front), typed by what they are. ollowing are suggestions for pronouncing Book of Mormon names and
annotations.note: Pronunciation Guide — a glossary of Book of Mormon proper-name pronunciations (alphabetized A→Z headword list with phonetic respellings, e.g. 'Aaron\u2003ĕr´an'), introduced by 'Following are suggestions for pronouncing Book of Mormon names and terms…'. Sits at ~offset 1.849M, immediately after the Book of Mormon body/footnote apparatus and before the Doctrine and Covenants. Type=glossary (per-term gloss list). NOTE on edges: the heading repeats 6× in reference_text() — 2 are the front-matter contents/TOC ('Pronunciation Guide . . . .'), 1 is this section start, and 3 are running page headers ('Pronunciation Guide 534/535/536'); the start_anchor with its 'Following are suggestions…' continuation resolves uniquely. end_anchor=<<EOF>> is a placeholder edge: this is a single-section presence annotation, the true end is just before the D&C front matter; per the schema NOTE, per-instance EDGES for idx101 are not the rated quantity (A3 scores presence/recall), and a clean unique END token interior to the dense A→Z respelling list is not reliably isolable. Caveat: the geometry constants in lds_columnar.py are tuned to the 2-column verse body; the Pronunciation Guide is a multi-column glossary, so column ordering within entry blocks may be locally imperfect (visible as the Key fragments interleaving the A-entries), though headwords remain readable and alphabetical.

annotations.note: Church History Maps — a back-matter appendix of historical maps with an explanatory intro ('The following maps can help you to better understand the early history of The Church…') followed by the alphabetical 'Church History Maps Index' of place names (Connecticut River 1:D1, etc.). The map images themselves are non-textual and skipped at extraction — only the intro prose and the map-index place list are in reference_text(). end_anchor 'Church History Maps Index' marks the sub-index header. JUDGMENT CALL: appendix vs back_matter — chose appendix because the section is supplementary illustrative material grouped under the printed 'Appendix' label, matching the spec's preference for specific types. Caveat: the columnar geometry parser is tuned to the 2-column verse body, not the map/photo pages; the map-index place list (multi-column) and the running 'Index 412 Church History Maps' header fragments interleave the entries, so within-page column order here is approximate.
